analysis.account: exact chronological cash sum of taken episodes; capital is the negative minimum of the cumulative path; an open final episode adds the formal envelope [cash, cash + W(1 - f)] under A1-A3
analysis.busy: an episode keeps the account busy until its closing attempt (closed), its entry instant (entry_closed, entry_unfilled) or the event bound (open classes); not_admitted_size and entry classes at or after the event bound leave it flat
analysis.claims: secondary and predeclared; never pooled with the primary or sensitivity results; displayed conditional evaluation only
analysis.policy: one account per route at zero fees; the primary entry decisions in time order; a decision is taken only when the account is flat at its decision instant; taken episodes are the engine episodes
analysis.unknown: a work cap, the episode cap or an exhausted step budget makes the account state unknown; later decisions are skipped_unknown and the account figures are a labelled prefix

input: the same once-only input seal reports/hip4-independent-research/q357-input-seal-v1.json, verified by pr.verify_seal

predeclaration.budget: projection <= 16384 B and receipts (including failure and pending copies) <= 8192 B in the secondary_sequential_projection_and_receipt category of the pinned amendment
predeclaration.failure: a complete route whose account cash is <= 0 or whose final state is open; for this window only
predeclaration.pooling: secondary; never pooled with the primary or sensitivity results
predeclaration.question: For one account per route at zero fees, taking the primary entry decisions in time order only when flat, how many decisions are taken or skipped, how do taken episodes end, and what are the exact account cash, capital and final state?
predeclaration.success: candidate_conditional: a complete route whose account cash is > 0 with a flat final state; reported with every count, capital and the envelope, never as fill, executability or profit
predeclaration.unavailable: admission unavailable, any refusal or hard limit, an incomplete scan, or a prefix after a work cap or episode cap; never converted to a negative
